title: Bounded cosimplicial replacements in a combinatorial model category
statement: Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A model category is combinatorial when its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems have small generating sets. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Locally $\lambda$-presentable means generated under these colimits by a small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. A cosimplicial resolution means a Reedy cofibrant functor $A^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ whose structure maps are weak equivalences. Its canonical augmentation to $\operatorname{const}(A^0)$ is induced by the unique maps $[n]\to[0]$. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial. There exist an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$, a small full representative category $B$ of the $\lambda$-presentable objects, and a functorial cofibrant replacement $Q\to\mathrm{id}$ such that $\mathcal M$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable, $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserve objectwise weak equivalences, and $Q$ preserves $\lambda$-presentable objects. Put $C=B^{\mathrm{cof}}$. Let $E$ be a small model of the full category of cosimplicial objects with cofibrant $\lambda$-presentable terms. There is a functor $R:E\to E$ with a natural objectwise weak equivalence $\eta_A:RA\to A$ such that $RA$ is Reedy cofibrant, $(RA)^0=A^0$, and $\eta_A^0=1_{A^0}$. Constant diagrams on $C$ are objects of $E$. All representative choices and transports can be fixed functorially, keeping the specified degree-zero identifications. The full subcategory $D\subset E$ of cosimplicial resolutions is small; $R$ carries every object of $D$, and every constant diagram on an object of $C$, into $D$. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i)-(iii), Remark 2.5, Propositions 7.1-7.3, and the bounded Reedy replacement R in the proof of Lemma 6.3, printed pp. 179-180, 189-193. Only an existential regular bound is asserted. The sentence in Lemma 6.3 saying trivial cofibrations after the cofibration is a typo: use trivial fibrations. No Stacks tag states this model-category result. Sources read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Choose a regular cardinal kappa witnessing local presentability of M, with a small kappa-presentable generating family G. By the weak-equivalence accessibility theorem choose a regular cardinal kappa_W for closure of W in the arrow category. Apply the accessible small-object theorem to the chosen generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations. Their weakly saturated left classes are the model-category left classes: the cited lifting-closure and transfinite-lifting theorems put the weakly saturated class generated by I inside the model left class. Conversely factor f = p i in the model left class by the small-object construction. Since p is in the model right class, a filler h in the square with left edge f, right edge p, top edge i and bottom edge the identity satisfies h f = i and p h = 1. The arrow maps (1,h):f -> i and (1,p):i -> f exhibit f as a retract of i. Obtain functorial factorizations of both kinds, with middle-object functors F_1,F_2 preserving sufficiently filtered colimits. Choose an infinite regular alpha at least kappa, kappa_W and their two preservation ranks, using the regular-bound node. An alpha-filtered category is filtered at each of these smaller ranks. Thus both F_i preserve alpha-filtered colimits, W is closed under them, and every Hom(G,-) preserves them.

source.place: Proposition 2.3(i)-(iii), Proposition 7.1 and the setup of Proposition 7.2, printed pp. 179, 192.

proof.text: For every finite category J, Fun(J,M) is locally presentable by the presheaf local-presentability node applied to J^op; M has pullbacks by its model-category hypotheses. This includes the arrow category and the empty diagram category. The functor lim_J:Fun(J,M) -> M preserves alpha-filtered colimits: for a diagram X:I -> Fun(J,M) and G in the generating family, Hom(G,-) applied to the canonical comparison colim_i lim_j X(i,j) -> lim_j colim_i X(i,j) gives the bijection colim_i lim_j Hom(G,X(i,j)) = lim_j colim_i Hom(G,X(i,j)), by the cited finite-limit/filtered-colimit theorem for sets. The family G detects isomorphisms: if Hom(G,f) is bijective for all G, expressing an arbitrary Z as a colimit of members of G makes Hom(Z,f) a limit of bijections; taking Z to be the source and target supplies the inverse of f. Hence the comparison is an isomorphism, including when J is empty. This proves accessibility of the finite-limit functors; it does not assert that finite limits preserve presentability at the original rank.

source.place: Agent expansion of the cardinal control needed in Lemma 6.3, printed pp. 189-190; uses the cited set commutation theorem and ordinary Hom/limit universal properties.

proof.text: Apply the accessible-functor rank theorem to F_1,F_2 on the arrow category, to the identity of M, and to lim_J for one representative of each finite category J. These functor categories are locally presentable by step 2. There are countably many finite category structures, so the regular-bound node gives a common infinite regular sigma at least alpha and all the resulting rho ranks. Choose a regular lambda with sigma << lambda using the arbitrarily-large-sharp-rank clause of the rank theorem. For each of our functors rho << lambda follows from rho <= sigma. Thus M is locally lambda-presentable and all those functors preserve lambda-presentable objects. A finite J-diagram with lambda-presentable components is lambda-presentable in Fun(J,M): its natural-transformation Hom set is the equalizer of the two maps from the finite product over objects j of Hom(X_j,Y_j) to the finite product over arrows (j -> k) of Hom(X_j,Y_k). Pointwise colimits and the cited commutation theorem show that this equalizer preserves lambda-filtered colimits. In particular an arrow with presentable endpoints is presentable in the arrow category. Consequently the chosen F_i take arrows with lambda-presentable endpoints to lambda-presentable middle objects, and finite limits of lambda-presentable objects are lambda-presentable at this chosen lambda. Finite colimits also preserve lambda-presentability: Hom out of such a colimit is a finite limit of Hom sets, to which the same set commutation theorem applies. The initial object is lambda-presentable by its constant singleton Hom functor. Factoring 0 -> X with F_1 therefore defines a functorial cofibrant replacement QX -> X preserving lambda-presentables. Since lambda >= kappa_W, W is closed under lambda-filtered ambient arrow colimits, exactly the required objectwise weak-equivalence clause.

source.place: Proposition 2.3 and Proposition 7.2, printed pp. 179, 192; common sharp-rank refinement from the cited rank theorem, with explicit control of finite matching limits for Lemma 6.3.

proof.text: Choose a small lambda-presentable generating family H supplied by local lambda-presentability. Any lambda-presentable object X is a retract of a member H_i: in a lambda-filtered presentation X = colim_i H_i, presentability factors 1_X through one coprojection H_i -> X. Retracts of a fixed H_i up to isomorphism are classified by those idempotents in the small set Hom(H_i,H_i) that split: two splittings of the same idempotent are isomorphic by composing the retraction of either with the section of the other. Thus the lambda-presentable objects have a small set of representatives; this is the essential-smallness clause of the canonical-density theorem, whose hypothesis (every object a small lambda-filtered colimit of a fixed small family of lambda-presentable objects) is the local lambda-presentability just obtained. Choose a small full category B on representatives, and put C = B^cof. Cofibrancy is invariant under isomorphism by the lifting definition, so C represents exactly the cofibrant lambda-presentables. No assertion that Q takes values literally in the chosen B is needed.

source.place: Definition 2.2 and the following property (2), printed p. 179; the retract/idempotent argument supplies the smallness details.

proof.text: Set E = Fun(Delta,C), considered fully faithfully in the cosimplicial category of M. This is small: its objects are a subset of the product of the object set of C over the countable object set of Delta and the product of the corresponding Hom sets over its arrows, cut out by the functor equations; its morphisms are families in a small product of Hom sets cut out by naturality equations. It models all cosimplicial objects with cofibrant lambda-presentable terms: choose isomorphisms from each term to a representative in C and conjugate every structure map by these isomorphisms; conjugate natural-transformation components in the same way. This preserves identity and composition since adjacent isomorphisms cancel. Every constant diagram on C is literally in E.

source.place: Setup of Lemma 6.3, printed p. 189; explicit representative model of its category E.

proof.text: For A in E construct a raw factorization 0 -> Z(A) -> A by Reedy induction, using the chosen functorial cofibration--trivial-fibration factorization F_1. In degree zero use 0 -> A^0 followed by 1_(A^0): the first map is a cofibration since A^0 is cofibrant, and the second is a trivial fibration. Suppose the partial factorization is defined below n, where n > 0. Form the map L_n Z -> A^n times_(M_n A) M_n Z and factor it by F_1. The latching and matching indexing categories at [n] consist of proper injections into [n] and proper surjections from [n]; both have finitely many objects and morphisms, all at degrees below n. By induction and step 3, L_n Z, M_n A and M_n Z are lambda-presentable, as is their displayed pullback with A^n. The middle object Z(A)^n is therefore lambda-presentable. The relative latching map is a cofibration and the relative matching map is a trivial fibration. The Reedy extension theorem supplies all structure maps and extends the factorization functorially. Induction gives a Reedy cofibrant Z(A) and a Reedy trivial fibration epsilon_A:Z(A) -> A, hence an objectwise weak equivalence. Its terms are cofibrant by the objectwise consequence of the Reedy theorem, so every term has a representative in C. In degree zero Z(A)^0 = A^0 and epsilon_A^0 = 1.

source.place: Lemma 6.3 construction, printed pp. 189-190, using the relative latching/matching extension statement of the cited Reedy node. The printed trivial-cofibration phrase is replaced by trivial fibration.

proof.text: Fix for each cofibrant lambda-presentable object X a representative r(X) in C with an isomorphism u_X:X -> r(X); this choice can be made in the larger universe permitted in the statement. For each A in E put (RA)^0 = A^0, u_(A,0) = 1, and (RA)^n = r(Z(A)^n), u_(A,n) = u_(Z(A)^n) for n > 0. Define RA(beta) = u_(A,n) Z(A)(beta) u_(A,m)^(-1) for beta:[m] -> [n]. For f:A -> A' define (Rf)^n = u_(A',n) Z(f)^n u_(A,n)^(-1). Cancellation of adjacent inverse isomorphisms proves the cosimplicial identities, naturality, and the identity and composition laws for R:E -> E. Put eta_A^n = epsilon_A^n u_(A,n)^(-1); the same formulas give naturality of eta in both A and the simplex operators. The maps u assemble an isomorphism of diagrams Z(A) -> RA, so the lifting definitions preserve Reedy cofibrancy under this isomorphism and eta is an objectwise weak equivalence. In degree zero the specified formulas are literal identities. These formulas supply the functorial representative transports rather than assuming that a choice of representatives is itself a functor.

source.place: Explicit representative transport of the construction in Lemma 6.3, printed pp. 189-190.

proof.text: Let D be the full subcategory of E on Reedy cofibrant objects whose every structure map is a weak equivalence; it is small as a full subcategory of E. If A is in D and beta:[m] -> [n], naturality gives eta_A^n (RA)(beta) = A(beta) eta_A^m. Both eta components and A(beta) are weak equivalences. Two-out-of-three first makes the right-hand composite a weak equivalence and then makes (RA)(beta) a weak equivalence. If A is constant on c in C, its map A(beta) is 1_c, a weak equivalence, and the identical two-out-of-three calculation applies. In both cases RA is already Reedy cofibrant by step 7, so RA is in D. The augmentation to const(A^0) has components A([n] -> [0]); uniqueness of these simplex maps proves naturality. All constructions used ordinary limits, colimits, factorizations and representative isomorphisms, so no simplicial enrichment was assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.3, printed pp. 189-190, and the definition of cosimplicial resolution used there.
